# NoTime — Phase 1 technical document

**Team:** NoTime · **Repository:** https://github.com/isaad18/more-than-a-hack-2027 (code in `solution/`)
**Submission:** `NoTime.csv`, regenerated byte-for-byte by `python solution/run.py`

## 1. Approach in one paragraph

We treat possession as a sequence problem, not a per-frame one. A gradient-boosted tree model
estimates, for every frame, the probability that the home team has the ball, the away team has
it, or the ball is dead. It learns from positional features only: whole-pitch movement, team
shape, ball–player distances, and "how long since / until each team last / next touched the
ball". A three-state hidden Markov model then decodes those probabilities with Viterbi. It
charges a fixed cost for every change of state, so possessions come out whole instead of
flickering. The model is trained only on three other matches that Metrica publishes openly. Their
ball is deliberately hidden the way BAR-ATH loses it, so the model learns to work without a ball.

```
ATD tracking ──► features (per frame) ──► P(H), P(A), P(D) ──► Viterbi (H/A/D, switch costs) ──► NoTime.csv
                   motion, team shape,      gradient-boosted       one path per half
                   touches before/after,    trees, trained on
                   ball context             3 external games
```

## 2. Why this design

We started with a rule-based v0: nearest player within 1.5 m, plus a confirmation window. It beat
the published baseline, but two facts about the BAR-ATH tracking shaped everything after it:

1. **The ball is missing in long blocks during live play.** Inside the halves there are only 149
   missing-ball stretches. Their median length is 11 s and the longest is 3.7 minutes. A "ball
   missing → dead ball" rule labelled 43% of the match dead, against roughly 20% in reality.
2. **Player movement separates live play from stoppages, and it carries over between matches.**
   The median of the mean player speed is about 2 m/s during play and about 1 m/s during a
   stoppage. That holds in all three development games and in BAR-ATH alike.
   With no ball at all, **team shape** (the side in possession pushes up and spreads out)
   identifies the team in possession about 79% of the time on held-out games.

So the ball cannot be the backbone. The model has to combine ball evidence where the ball exists
with whole-team evidence everywhere else. And because the ranking metric (spellF1) rewards
*whole* possessions, the per-frame evidence must be decoded into sequences rather than
thresholded frame by frame.

## 3. Assets: used and dropped

| Asset | Used? | How / why not |
|---|---|---|
| Tactical ATD (`_atd.txt` + `_atd.xml`) | **Yes** | All player and ball positions; track slot → team from the metadata. `video_frame = frame_id − 1`. Coordinates × (105.3, 68.0) m. Ball speed is recomputed from positions (the file's column is always NaN). |
| Smart Tagging | No (dropped) | The development games have no Smart Tagging, so any rule built on it could not be validated without touching BAR-ATH labels. Throw-ins also carry `Team = N/A`. It is the obvious next input (§7). |
| Homography, tactical video | No | We use tracking only; we did not run our own detection. |
| Broadcast ATD / video | No | Not frame-aligned to the tactical video and a third of it has no homography. |
| Public 5-minute ground truth | Only as a bug alarm | Used to check alignment and file format. **No constant was chosen on it.** |

## 4. Training data

| Dataset | Source | Who labelled it | Amount |
|---|---|---|---|
| Metrica Sports Sample Games 1, 2, 3 | https://github.com/metrica-sports/sample-data (public) | Event data annotated and released by Metrica Sports; possession labels **derived mechanically** by our rule below | 3 matches, 428,169 graded frames (~4.8 h of play) |

No labels of any kind from the competition game (BAR-ATH) were used for training, validation or
tuning. No person labelled anything for this project.

**Event → per-frame label rule** (fixed before any scoring; `solution/external.py`):
- **Dead** from a `BALL OUT` (its end frame, when the ball crosses the line), a `FAULT RECEIVED`,
  or a goal, until the next `SET PIECE`.
- **While alive**, the ball belongs to the team of the latest `PASS`, `CARRY`, `SHOT`, `RECOVERY`
  or `SET PIECE`. `BALL LOST` and `CHALLENGE` never move possession by themselves; only the other
  team's next action does.

**Making the external games look like BAR-ATH.** The sample tracking loses the ball mostly during
stoppages, which makes "ball missing" a near-perfect dead-ball signal there but not in BAR-ATH.
We therefore hide each development game's ball in alternating visible/missing stretches drawn
from **BAR-ATH's own run-length distribution**. That uses tracking statistics only, never labels.
It is seeded, so it is deterministic. Training uses three masks per game (seeds 1011–1033);
evaluation uses a different mask (seed = game number).

## 5. The possession rules we implemented

- **Touch** (`rules.py`): a team is "on the ball" in a frame if its nearest player is within
  **1.5 m** and the opposing nearest player is not within 0.5 m of that distance; otherwise
  contested/nobody. A touch is *evidence*, not possession.
- **Control vs. touch.** The model sees frames since and until each team's touches, capped at 60 s.
  So a single opposing touch followed by our own team on the ball again (a deflection, a lost
  aerial duel) is weak evidence of a change, while an opposing touch followed by more opposing
  touches (a completed pass) is strong. Looking ahead is legitimate because the whole match is
  available offline. This is our reading of "a team completes more than two consecutive passes".
- **Loose and contested ball stays with the last team.** In the HMM, staying in the same state is
  free and changing team costs **30** (log-units). A short spell of ambiguous evidence therefore
  never flips possession.
- **Dead ball.** Entering or leaving D costs **15**. D is driven mainly by whole-pitch motion
  (everyone slows down while a restart is set up), by the ball near or beyond a line before it
  vanishes, and by the length of the ball's absence. We do not predict dead-ball "ownership",
  as the challenge asks.
- **Restarts.** After D, the decoder enters whichever team the evidence favours: the team on the
  ball when it reappears and its shape.
- **Halves** are decoded independently; everything outside them is `X`. There is **no `X` inside
  the halves**.

The two costs were chosen by grid search on held-out development games (§6). Only the ratio of
costs to evidence matters, so the evidence weight is fixed at 1. The switch cost equals twice the
dead cost: above that, the decoder would switch teams through a one-frame D instead.

## 6. Results

Development games, each scored with a model trained on the **other two** (out-of-sample), using
the official `possession_metrics.py`:

| Version | spellF1 | macroF1 |
|---|---|---|
| v0 — nearest-player rules + confirmation window | 0.445 | 0.645 |
| v1 — two logistic regressions (motion, shape) + touches, HMM | 0.465 | 0.741 |
| **v2 — gradient-boosted frame model + HMM (submitted)** | **0.587** | **0.800** |

Per game, v2 scores 0.570 / 0.568 / 0.623 spellF1. Labels on these games are our event-derived
proxy, so absolute numbers are not comparable with BAR-ATH; the comparison between versions is
what they are for.

Output on BAR-ATH: 339 possessions, mean 13.0 s, home share of alive time 57.7%, D 30.8% of
graded frames, no `X` inside the halves.

## 7. Limitations and what we would do next

- **Too much D on BAR-ATH** (30.8% against roughly 20% expected). The event-derived labels count a
  stoppage from the ball crossing the line until the restart is taken. That makes the
  development games' stoppages long (24–33% D), and the model inherits this. The organisers'
  definition, from corrected tracking, appears tighter.
- **Label proxy.** Our development labels are derived from events, while the organisers' are
  derived from corrected tracking. "Control" in particular may be timed differently, e.g.
  recovery at first touch rather than once control is established.
- **Smart Tagging is unused.** Set-piece instances mark restarts and could sharpen D boundaries;
  validating that needs a development source with tagging.
- **Only three development games.** With more labelled games, we would tune per-feature and
  calibrate probabilities rather than rely on a single evidence weight.
- **No ball re-detection.** Running a detector on the tactical video to fill the 41% of missing
  ball frames would help most, at a large engineering cost.
- **Track fragmentation** (46 slots, ~20.5 players per frame, identity switches) is not repaired;
  we only use collective, identity-free features for that reason.

## 8. Reproduction

Python 3.11. From a clone of the repository with the match bundle unpacked into `data/` (or
`MTAH_DATA_DIR` pointing at it):

```bash
python -m venv .venv && .venv/bin/pip install -r solution/requirements.txt
.venv/bin/python solution/run.py                     # -> evaluation/results/NoTime.csv (~10 s)
.venv/bin/python evaluation/validate_submission.py evaluation/results/NoTime.csv
```

`run.py` uses the committed `solution/possession_model.pkl`. To rebuild everything from scratch,
including the model:

```bash
solution/get_external.sh                             # Metrica sample games -> data/external/
.venv/bin/python solution/classifier.py              # held-out check + retrain the model (~2 min)
.venv/bin/python solution/tune.py                    # decoder cost grid on held-out games
.venv/bin/python solution/dev_eval.py                # dev scores + BAR-ATH sanity checks
.venv/bin/python solution/run.py
```

We verified that a fresh copy with a new virtual environment and raw data only, and a full retrain,
both reproduce the identical file (MD5 `26a932514a583d70aa8e6542c4b96943`). No step uses
unseeded randomness.
